_about: Expected TASK TITLES for messages that route to create-task. Day 15.
WHY THIS EXISTS. Day 14b replaced a keyword router with a classifier, so phrasings
nobody wrote down now reach the title extractor — and the extractor was still a fixed
list of prefixes. Measured before the fix: 16 of these 32 messages matched NO prefix at
all and became their own title verbatim, which is not a task title, it is the message.
The classifier generalised the routing and left the naming behind. That defect was
created by Day 14b and is recorded as such.
THE MESSAGES ARE INDEPENDENT OF THIS FIX. Every one is copied from
evaluation/intent_train.json or evaluation/tool_cases.json, both written earlier and
for a different purpose — routing, not naming. Nothing was added here to suit an
algorithm. tests/test_title_extraction.py asserts that provenance, so a future case
invented to make a number look better fails the suite.
THE LABELS ARE MINE AND THEY ARE NEW, which is the honest limit of this set: the
inputs are held out, the expectations are not. They were written down BEFORE the
implementation changed, from the messages alone, and the baseline below was measured
against them afterwards. That ordering is the only thing stopping this from being a
record of whatever the code happens to do.
WHAT MAKES A GOOD TITLE HERE. It names the WORK, not the request. A task list is read
at a glance, so 'could you jot down that the hangar light is broken' should appear as
'The hangar light is broken' — the wrapper is how the user asked, not what they want
done. Two rules follow from that and are visible in the cases below:
* A REQUEST WRAPPER IS STRIPPED. 'please', 'can you', 'I need to', 'create a task
to', 'jot down that' — all scaffolding around the real content.
* A WORK VERB IS KEPT. 'follow up on the runway inspection' is the work; stripping
'follow up on' leaves 'The runway inspection', which names a topic rather than a
task. The old prefix list got this wrong in the opposite direction.
The boundary between the two is a judgement call and is where this set will be wrong
if it is wrong.
